name: Shelf Substrate: The Involuntary Trials of Ward Nine
description: Assembled over four years by anonymous documentarians using smuggled sensor rigs, this film documents HelixCorp's covert forced substrate migration trials conducted on unregistered Shelf residents in the Ward Nine medical annex between 2190 and 2195, including testimony from eleven survivors whose neural architectures were permanently altered without consent. The footage includes internal HelixCorp communications obtained through a whistleblower who disappeared six weeks before the film's initial underground release. It circulates exclusively on physical media — a single encrypted chip — because streaming any portion of it triggers corponation surveillance flags within seconds.
cultural_impact: The phrase 'Ward Nine' became underground shorthand for any covert corporate medical experiment, and the film's existence — even among people who have never seen it — functions as a persistent symbol of resistance in Shelf communities.
story_hooks: A character acquires what appears to be a copy of the chip but cannot verify its authenticity — and the act of verifying it may expose them to surveillance.

One of the eleven documented survivors is still alive and living openly, apparently unbothered — which either means HelixCorp considers them neutralized or there is something about their testimony they want suppressed.
A HelixCorp internal affairs investigator is quietly tasked with locating the fourth filmmaker, and the player must decide whose side to take.
